page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for parallel computing, machine learning inference, and graphics workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 372 GB of system memory, providing 3.88 GB per core. The graphics pipeline is backed by four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. Networking capabilities feature a 30 Gbps baseline bandwidth, though the instance carries no local ephemeral storage and relies on external block volumes.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a core tradeoff between single-threaded clock constraints and high parallel efficiency. Single-threaded performance shows lower throughput, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.89 and gzip compression throughput of 19.2 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is strong, achieving a stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 70574.45 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 287.37 GB/sec. In-memory operations demonstrate high efficiency for small, cached workloads, reaching 3924.63 GB/sec for 16 KB read blocks and achieving 64.27 million Redis SET operations per second, while uncached large-block memory read and write speeds remain in average performance tiers.

From a resource density perspective, bundling four T4 GPUs with 96 vCPUs creates high parallel compute capacity relative to system management overhead. Because the instance lacks attached local SSD storage, operational IOPS depend on network-attached storage, supported by the 30 Gbps network interface. The instance is suited for multi-GPU machine learning inference, video transcoding pipelines, parallel scientific simulations, high-concurrency Redis caching layers, and batch data processing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance engineered for high-concurrency workloads and acceleration-driven processing. It features 96 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 372 GB of system memory. Acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs featuring a cumulative 64 GB of VRAM. The instance operates on KVM hypervisor architecture with a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and relies entirely on network storage due to having no local disk capacity. Benchmarks demonstrate substantial multi-core and cached memory performance, recording 70574.45 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 64.27 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, despite lower single-threaded clock performance. This instance fits multi-GPU deep learning inference, batch video transcoding, parallel analytics, and scalable caching services.
